items.hook: Tonina is a pre-Columbian archaeological site and ruined city of the Maya civilization located in what is now the Mexican state of Chiapas, some 13 km (8.1 mi) east of the town of Ocosingo.
items.body: One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Matsura Seizan , born Matsura Kiyoshi , was a daimyō, essayist, and famed swordsman during the Edo period of Japan.
items.body: Seizan was a practitioner of Iba Hideaki's Shingyōtō-ryū school of swordsmanship, in which Seizan was considered as an adept. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Mike D: ‘After Yauch died I couldn’t make music. I’d open a computer file and just feel sadness’
items.body: As part of the Beastie Boys, the rapper shot to fame and notoriety in the 80s, before bandmate Adam Yauch’s death saw him withdraw from the spotlight. He returns with a solo album that sees him reckon with greed, mortality – and his past

items.hook: A split-finger fastball or splitter is an off-speed pitch in baseball that initially looks like a fastball from the batters perspective, but then drops suddenly.
items.body: Derived from the forkball, it is aptly named because the pitcher puts the index and middle finger on different sides of the ball. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Muttahida Qaumi Movement – Pakistan (MQM–P) is a Pakistani political party with a liberal political position and a Muhajir nationalist ideology.
items.body: The leader of the party is Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui. The world is stranger than it lets on.
